div.head: II Ew 5
div.ab: Gif hwa ðis oferhebbe ⁊ his að ⁊ his wæd brece, ðe eal ðeod geseald hæfð, bete swa dómboc tæce.
Gyf hwa ðis oferhebbe ⁊ his að ⁊ his wed brece, ðe heal ðeod geseald hæfð, bete swa domboc tæce.
Si quis hoc superhabeat et iuramentum suum frangat et uadium, quod omnis populus contulit, emendet sicut liber iudicialis dicit.
[Be ðon ðe ful friþiaþ.] Gif hwa ðis oferhebbe ⁊ his að ⁊ his wæd brece, ðe eal ðeod geseald hæfð, bete swa dómboc tæce.
Wenn einer dies übertritt und [so] seinen Eid und sein Versprechen bricht, die das ganze Volk [dem Staat] gegeben hat, so büsse er, wie das Gesetzbuch vorschreibt.
If anyone transgresses this and [so] breaks his oath and his pledge, which the whole people has given [to the state], let him pay compensation as the law-book prescribes.
If anyone neglects this and breaks his oath and his pledge, [an oath and pledge] which the whole nation has given, he shall pay such compensation as the written laws declare.

note.label: refers to
note.quote: yet II Ew 5 pretty clearly refers to Af 1, whose ramifications can be shown to extend to theft

note.label: alludes to (but modifies)
note.quote: Edward’s clause is one of several that allude to the domboc. But it may not ... be assumed that Edward’s understanding of að and wedd is the same as that underlying Alfred §1.

note.label: fills gap left by
note.quote: Could this singular text then have been drafted by someone who spotted the gap left by what Edward expected of his treaties? [n. II Ew 4 – 5:2]

Hier scheint der Grundherr gemeint, ja sogar ‘dies’ das ganze Stück 1, 2—4 zu umfassen, nicht etwa nur an Diebeshelfer aus der letzten Zeile gedacht. Denn 5, 2 bezeichnet den Übertreter nicht als Begünstiger von Verbrechen, sondern behandelt ihn nur solchem gleich

The landlord seems to be meant here; indeed ‘this’ seems to cover the whole piece 1, 2—4, and not, say, to refer only to the abettors of thieves in the last line. For 5, 2 does not describe the transgressor as an abettor of crime, but merely treats him as equivalent to one
superhabere ist Q’s silbenhafte Übs. für oferhebban und ofer habban; s. Wb
superhabere is Q’s syllable-by-syllable translation of oferhebban and ofer habban; see Wb
‘Eid und Versprechen’ Ein Begriff
‘Oath and pledge’ is a single concept
Unorganisch h-, in B nicht selten, s. Wb S. 107
Inorganic h-, not uncommon in B, see Wb p. 107

Nicht etwa jene Gefolgschaftsverbindung zwischen König und Witan in 1, 1 kann gemeint sein, sondern ein Ehrlichkeitsversprechen (s. d. Gl 3a—4a; Volk 4b. 5) aller Untertanen, dessen Wortlaut aus nächster Generation erhalten ist

What is meant cannot be, say, the bond of following between king and witan in 1, 1, but rather a pledge of honesty (see that word in Gl 3a—4a; Volk 4b. 5) given by all subjects, the wording of which survives from the next generation
Da Spurfolge in Af-Ine nicht vorkommt, muss sich das Zitat auf den Bruch eidlichen Versprechens (s. d. Gl 3f. 6) beziehen
Since pursuit of the trail does not occur in Af-Ine, the citation must refer to breach of a sworn pledge (see that word in Gl 3f. 6)
Probably, as Liebermann suggests, the two words express only one idea.

For domboc, see note 1 to I Edw. Preamble. Liebermann points out that as there is nothing in the Laws of Ine or of Alfred about tracing stolen cattle, the reference to the domboc can be relevant only to the breaking of a man’s oath and pledge (cf. Alf. cap. 1 § 2; cap. 7). ðis (Gif hwa ðis oferhebbe) probably refers to all the preceding sections (cf. II As. cap. 25), and not to cap. 4 only.
